los.text: Perform a rapid A to E (Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability, Exposure) assessment on a critically ill patient.
los.html:
• Rapid A–E in a critically ill patient (see ICM Year 1 › Emergencies & A–E › LO 15): call for help early
    • monitoring
    • treat as you go
    • reassess
    • escalate.
Hypovolaemia at C
Tachycardia, narrow pulse pressure, cool peripheries, CRT >2 s, hypotension (late), low urine output, confusion
Two large-bore cannulae (14–16G), bloods (FBC, crossmatch, clotting, lactate, VBG)
Fluid bolus: 500 mL crystalloid over <15 min; reassess; blood if haemorrhage
Find and stop the cause (bleeding, vomiting, diarrhoea, burns, DKA)

los.text: Demonstrate an awareness of the emergency management of haemorrhage, including identification and treatment.
los.html:
Haemorrhage management
  • Recognise: visible bleeding
  • Signs of shock
  • Hidden sources (chest, abdomen, pelvis, long bones, "blood on the floor and four more")
  • GI bleed (haematemesis, melaena)
Control: direct pressure, elevation, tourniquet (limbs), pelvic binder, reverse anticoagulants
  • Resuscitate: large-bore access
  • Activate the major haemorrhage protocol
  • Blood products (red cells, plasma, platelets in ratio)
  • Tranexamic acid within 3 h (trauma)
  • Avoid too much crystalloid (dilution, coagulopathy)
Permissive hypotension in trauma (until bleeding controlled)
Definitive: surgery, endoscopy, interventional radiology
Monitor: lactate, Hb, clotting, calcium, temperature (avoid the lethal triad: hypothermia, acidosis, coagulopathy)

los.text: Demonstrate increased confidence and competence in performing intimate examinations, ensuring appropriate communication, consent, and patient dignity throughout the procedure.
los.html:
• Intimate examination standards (see ICM Year 1 › Gastrointestinal & liver › LO 8): explanation
    • consent
    • chaperone
    • privacy
    • talk through each step
    • stop if asked
    • dignity
    • document.

los.text: Perform a full gynaecological examination on a model, including the collection of swabs and cervical smears.
los.html: • Speculum and bimanual with swabs and smear: see ICM Year 1 › Reproductive & sexual health › LO 1.

los.text: Perform a clinical examination of the hip with increased confidence and clinical accuracy.
los.html:
• Hip examination: see ICM Year 1 › Musculoskeletal › LOs 10 and 14
    • aim for fluency, accurate leg length and rotation, Trendelenburg and Thomas's tests.

los.text: Perform a clinical examination of the knee with increased confidence and clinical accuracy.
los.html: • Knee examination: see ICM Year 1 › Musculoskeletal › LO 7; effusion tests, ligament and meniscal tests with clear explanations.

los.text: Perform a clinical examination of the shoulder with increased confidence and clinical accuracy.
los.html: • Shoulder examination: see ICM Year 1 › Musculoskeletal › LO 1; rotator cuff tests, impingement, ACJ, compare passive external rotation.

los.text: Complete a thorough musculoskeletal clinical examination within 6.5 minutes, ensuring efficiency and accuracy.
los.html:
MSK exam in 6.5 minutes
Intro and exposure (30 s)
Look standing, including gait (1 min)
Feel systematically (1 min)
Move: active then passive (1.5 min)
Special tests: the most relevant 2–3 (1.5 min)
Neurovascular check, joint above and below (30 s)
Summary to the examiner (30 s)

los.text: Identify the importance of social history, including patient behaviours that may contribute to illness.
los.html:
Social historyWhy it matters
Smoking (pack-years)Lung, cardiovascular, cancer risk
Alcohol (units/week, CAGE/AUDIT)Liver disease, falls, withdrawal
Recreational drugsInfection, cardiac, psychiatric
Diet and exerciseObesity, diabetes, CVD
OccupationAsbestos, dust, stress, injury
Home and functionDischarge planning, falls, carers
Sexual behaviourSTIs
TravelInfection
  • Behaviours contributing to illness are modifiable: opportunity for health promotion.

los.text: Explain a diagnosis to a patient
los.html:
• Explaining a diagnosis (see ICM Year 1 › History taking & communication › LO 20): find out what they know
    • chunk and check
    • plain language
    • discuss what it means for them
    • treatment options
    • safety-netting
    • teach-back
    • written information.
